scope: GUI automation session lifetime; no production app source changes
implementation: Tests/gui-session.mjs retires its wrapped App before a final Quit action; all saved wrapper references reject subsequent observation/input locally, including during a pending or failed response. Caller confirms PID exit before binding a new session.
guiMethod: Computer Use through explicit app-path sessions; native Open, Save, Window-close and Quit controls; Finder Open Finder item; screenshot inspection

checks: Click second document to enter editing without changing it
Command-W closes second editing window and first window remains accessible
saved wrapper getAXState rejected before CUA call
Rebind only after first PID exit
Open one.md, edit, Quit, Cancel, further typing and Undo
Open two.md, edit, Save and close; first window remains accessible
Quit and Don’t Save first document
saved wrapper getAXState rejected before CUA call
After second PID exit, Finder opens the isolated .app; new PID is confirmed before CUA binding
Open two.md and verify saved text
Close last document: noWindowsAvailable observed, PID remains alive and previews are already cleaned
Command-N on the same live session opens a responsive empty document
saved wrapper getScreenshot rejected before CUA call

systemLogFilter: CoreServicesUIAgent records for the test bundle/name and direct main-app launchd termination lines; unrelated XPC-service lifecycle noise excluded

files.two.md: saved edited Markdown verified on disk and after relaunch

limitations: The 2026-10-26 Finder popup itself was not independently reproduced or captured; the historical log confirms a reopen AppleEvent sent at process termination.
The persistent CUA timeout from 2026-11-07 did not recur. Its exact host-side cause is unconfirmed; a current noWindowsAvailable alone was verified to be a normal windowless app, not a deadlock.
The helper only protects calls made through its session wrapper. Raw CUA handles, other callers and fresh bindings still require the documented lifecycle procedure.
Installed app/Gatekeeper policy and macOS 14 hardware are unchanged and untested.
